en: to be opened to the public (museum, library)

examples.en: The new art museum opens next week.
This library was opened in 1998.

examples.ko: 박물관이 개관된 지 벌써 십 년이 지났어요.
examples.en: It has already been ten years since the museum opened.
The science museum for citizens has finally opened.

examples.ko: 개관되기 전에 직원들이 청소를 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: Before the opening, the staff cleaned hard.
When is this exhibition hall scheduled to open?

explain: 개관되다는 도서관·박물관·미술관·전시관처럼 '관'이 붙은 곳이 문을 열 때만 써요. 가게나 식당은 '개업하다', '오픈하다'라고 해요. 문을 여는 사람이 주어이면 '개관하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 새 박물관은 다음 달 개관 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new museum is scheduled to open next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열 날짜를 안내할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in announcements about the opening date.

phrases.en: As soon as the art museum opened, many people came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열 곳이 주어일 때 '개관되다'를 쓰고, 문을 연 바로 그때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 개관되다 when the place that opens is the subject; this phrase means right at the moment of opening.

phrases.en: The new art museum opened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 문을 열다 is easier and more common.

explain_en: 개관되다 is only for places whose names end in 관, such as a library, museum or exhibition hall. Shops and restaurants use 개업하다 or 오픈하다 instead. If the person opening it is the subject, use 개관하다.

dis.h: a museum or library is opened

p.n: 개장 is for outdoor places like beaches or markets, not libraries.

examples.en: The illegally parked car was towed.
My car broke down, so I called a tow.
The towing fee was more expensive than I expected.
A tow truck came and took the car away.
Towing is covered by insurance, so it is free.
A towing operation is going on on the road.

explain: 주로 차에 쓰는 말이라 '견인차', '견인료', '견인되다'로 많이 써요. 고장 났을 때는 '견인을 부르다', 불법 주차로 끌려갔을 때는 '견인당하다'라고 해요. '끌다'는 일상 말이고, 견인은 차를 끌고 가는 일에 쓰는 전문적인 말이에요.

phrases.example: 견인차가 와서 고장 난 차를 끌고 갔어요.
phrases.en: A tow truck came and took the broken-down car away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 끌고 가는 차를 말해요. 길에서 사고가 났을 때 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The truck that tows cars; called when there is trouble on the road.

phrases.en: The towing fee was fifty thousand won.
phrases.nuance_en: The fee charged for towing a vehicle.

phrases.example: 제 차가 어제 견인돼서 찾으러 갔어요.
phrases.en: My car was towed yesterday, so I went to pick it up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 주어로 해서 끌려갔다는 말이에요. 불법 주차 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the car as the subject, meaning it was towed; common in talk about illegal parking.

explain_en: It is mostly used for cars: '견인차' (tow truck), '견인료' (towing fee), '견인되다' (get towed). After a breakdown you '견인을 부르다'; when towed for illegal parking you say '견인당하다'. '끌다' is the everyday word; 견인 is the technical term for towing a vehicle.

examples.en: The hull of the ship hit a rock and got scratched.
Water slowly came into the hull.
Large ships have their hulls made of steel.

examples.ko: 선체 길이가 삼백 미터나 되는 배예요.
examples.en: It is a ship with a hull three hundred meters long.

examples.ko: 수리 중이라서 선체에 페인트를 새로 칠했어요.
examples.en: It is under repair, so they repainted the hull.
Divers are inspecting the sunken hull.

explain: 배의 몸통 부분만 가리켜요. 배 전체는 '배'라고 하고, 큰 배를 격식 있게 부를 때는 '선박'이라고 해요. 사고 뉴스에서 '선체 인양'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Raising the hull began after the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가라앉은 배를 물 위로 끌어올릴 때 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news for lifting a sunken ship out of the water.

phrases.en: The hull tilted because of the strong wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배의 몸통이 한쪽으로 기운 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ship's body leaning to one side.

phrases.en: The damage to the hull was not big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고 뒤 배 몸통의 피해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for damage to the ship's body after an accident.

explain_en: It points only to the body of a ship. The whole vessel is 배, and 선박 is the formal word for a large ship. It often appears in accident news, as in 선체 인양 (raising the hull).

examples.ko: 그 사람은 경찰서 유치장에서 하룻밤을 보냈대요.
examples.en: I heard that person spent one night in the police station's holding cell.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 유치장에 갇히는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There's a scene in the movie where the main character is locked in a holding cell.
The police took the man to the holding cell.
I heard it's cold and dark inside a holding cell.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 유치장 환경이 좋지 않다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said the conditions in holding cells are poor.

examples.ko: 하룻밤 유치장 신세를 졌다고 친구가 웃으며 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said with a laugh that he spent a night in a holding cell.

explain: 경찰서 안에서 사람을 잠시 가두는 곳이에요. 재판을 받고 형이 정해진 사람이 지내는 '교도소'와는 달라서 둘을 구별해서 써야 해요. '유치장에 갇히다/넣다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 술에 취해 싸운 사람이 밤새 유치장에 갇혔어요.
phrases.en: The man who got into a drunken fight was held in a cell overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본인이 그곳에 가둬지는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is locked up there.
phrases.en_equiv: to be locked in a holding cell

phrases.en: The police put that person in a holding cell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 가두는 쪽의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of those who detain the person.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in a holding cell

phrases.example: 그는 다음 날 아침에 유치장에서 나왔어요.
phrases.en: He came out of the holding cell the next morning.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being released and coming out.
phrases.en_equiv: to get out of a holding cell

explain_en: It is a place inside a police station where a person is held for a short time. It differs from '교도소' (prison), where people serve a sentence after trial, so keep the two apart. It is used as '유치장에 갇히다/넣다'.

examples.en: The raising of the sunken ship has begun.
The salvage work took a month.
The salvage was postponed because of bad weather.
The salvage succeeded, and the families shed tears.
The raising of the ship and the investigation proceed separately.

examples.ko: 오랜 인양 끝에 유물이 바다 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: After a long salvage, the relics came up from the sea.

explain: '인양'은 물에 가라앉은 배, 차, 유물을 끌어올리는 일에 써요. 사람이나 작은 물건을 건질 때는 '건지다', '구조하다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 '선박 인양', '인양 작업'으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Raising a ship costs a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인양'과 가장 자주 함께 나오는 말로, 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word most often paired with 인양, common in news.

phrases.en: They finally succeeded in raising the sunken ship.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the raising work ended well.

phrases.en: The sunken ship was raised yesterday.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of what is being raised.

explain_en: '인양' is for raising sunken ships, cars or relics out of the water. For rescuing people or fishing out small things, use '건지다' or '구조하다'. In the news you often see '선박 인양' and '인양 작업'.

en: to sink; to collapse; to cave in

examples.ko: 도로가 갑자기 함몰돼서 차가 지나가지 못해요.
examples.en: The road suddenly caved in, so cars can't get through.
The ground may cave in, so please be careful.
The building's floor caved in because of the earthquake.

examples.ko: 빗물 때문에 지반이 함몰되는 일이 가끔 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the ground sinks because of rainwater.

examples.ko: 사고로 차 앞부분이 안쪽으로 함몰된 채 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The car stood there with its front caved inward from the accident.

examples.ko: 볼이 푹 함몰되어 보일 만큼 살이 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I lost so much weight that my cheeks look sunken.

explain: 땅, 도로, 건물 바닥처럼 표면이 안쪽으로 푹 꺼질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '꺼지다', '푹 들어가다'가 더 자연스럽고, '함몰되다'는 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요. 주어가 스스로 꺼지는 말이라 목적어는 없어요.

phrases.en: Construction has started to repair the sunken road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함몰되다'의 과거형 '함몰된'으로 이미 꺼진 곳을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form '함몰된' describes a place that has already sunk.

phrases.example: 공사를 해서 땅이 함몰되지 않도록 했어요.
phrases.en: They did construction so the ground would not cave in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 '꺼지지 않게 막다'라는 안전 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is often used in safety talk about preventing a collapse.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 바닥이 푹 꺼졌어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so the floor sank in.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a simpler, everyday way to say it in conversation.

explain_en: Use it when a surface such as ground, a road or a floor sinks inward. In daily talk '꺼지다' or '푹 들어가다' sounds more natural, while '함몰되다' appears in news and explanatory writing. It takes no object because the subject sinks by itself.
